findings.title: isinstance check never matches spawned processes, so hung or dead flushers are not killed
findings.body: The processes are created from `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so `mp_context.Process` returns a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (`context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for every real process. The kill in `_ensure_processes_alive` is therefore skipped. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now a hung flusher keeps running, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second flusher on the same shards. Two flushers can then flush and produce the same segments concurrently. The same check at line 346 in `join()` means spawned processes are never terminated there either. The check should be against `BaseProcess`, or the kill should be done for any process object that has `kill`/`terminate`.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: The test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, and the module imports `time` and calls `time.sleep`. The added `time.sleep(0.1)` ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") therefore returns immediately and does not wait. The test relies on `step.join()` to flush, so the intended delay never happens and the comment is misleading. The wait should use a real sleep or an explicit synchronization point.

findings.title: Flag help and default contradict the PR's 'one process per shard' design
findings.body: The PR description and the flusher docstring say the flusher spawns one process per Redis shard. But `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, and the help text says it 'Defaults to 1'. With the default, all shards of a consumer share one flusher process, which is not the behaviour the PR describes. Either the default or the documentation is wrong.

findings.title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument order
findings.body: `flusher_processes` is inserted between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe` in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__`. Any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it as `flusher_processes`, and the flusher will receive a callable as its process count. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making the arguments keyword-only, avoids this.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here but 'shard' elsewhere
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `"shards"`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and `flusher_unhealthy` use `"shard"`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss this timer, so the key should be consistent.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change included in the PR
findings.body: The CLAUDE.md change adds a 'hasattr() for unions' anti-pattern example. This has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. It should be split into its own PR or dropped so the change set stays focused.
